originality.rationale: Nearest prior is Das-Jha arXiv:2508.05361 (v2 Jan 2026, JPAA 2025): proves general necessary criterion h3(12l)=2 / Z/6xZ/3 subgroup for 3l cube sum with l=7 mod 9, plus positive-proportion non-cube-sum theorem. Its numerical content is only small l: Table 1 lists e.g. 43,61,79,151,367,439,619,727 for n=3l family and Examples 3.1-3.2 use l=547,67; full-text search shows none of [2113,2131,2203,2221,2239,2293,2311,2347,2383,2437] appears. Jha-Majumdar-Shingavekar 2207.12487 gives general phi-Selmer bounds and sample families/proportion, not this window. De-Majumdar-Mondal 2412.13022 gives structural p-Selmer vs relative p-class-group relation, no explicit witnesses for window. Values (3/l)_3 for l~2100-2440 and resulting h3/verdicts are not mechanically implied by the general theorems (both outcomes occur: 6x symbol!=1, 4x symbol=1) and require fresh computation. No LMFDB entry decides these large-conductor E_{-432n^2} (n~6300-7310) cube-sum verdicts. Hence six proved non-cube-sum witnesses n=6339,6717,6879,6933,7041,7311 are substantively new.

value.rationale: Headline judged separately from unfinished 10/10 survey per standard: partial 6/10 census honestly labeled partial does not erase headline. Object n=3l with l=7 mod 9 prime is the motivated Das-Jha congruence family where w(n)=1 for all n yet cube-sum status varies and parity is silent (classical Sylvester problem, BSD-parity hard case). Invariant (proved non-cube-sum via h3=1<2 obstruction) was motivated before computation, is not known or mechanically implied, and required exact computation. Six rigorous root-number-1 witnesses in a complete consecutive window beyond literature samples are independently retrievable facts reusable for BSD 3-part testing, Goldfeld sextic-twist checks, and Selmer-vs-class-group benchmarks as recognized in Das-Jha/JMS/De et al. programs. This is a narrow exact datum, not a general theorem, but qualifies under the stated rule for exact invariants of natural objects. Not a textbook restatement, mere parameter substitution, tiny unmotivated gain, or unexplained enumeration.
